examples.en: This car has really good power.

examples.ko: 저 선수는 파워는 있는데 기술이 부족해요.
examples.en: That player has power but lacks technique.
I turned the vacuum's power up to maximum.
She sings in a powerful voice.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 파워 넘치는 느낌이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like the energetic feel of this song.

examples.ko: 정부 내에서도 워낙 파워가 센 사람이라 쉽게 물러나지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: He is so powerful even within the government that he won't step down easily.

explain: '힘'은 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '파워'는 기계 성능이나 시원하게 센 느낌, 영향력을 말할 때 주로 써요. 사람의 영향력이 클 때 '파워가 있다'고 해요. 몸이 약할 때는 '파워가 없다'보다 '힘이 없다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '힘' is the everyday word for strength, while 파워 is used for machine performance, a strong punchy feel, or influence. A person with great influence 'has 파워'. When you are physically weak, 힘이 없다 sounds more natural than 파워가 없다.

examples.en: I hope my injured leg recovers soon.
Health recovers slowly after surgery.
After resting a few days, my strength recovered a lot.

examples.ko: 경제가 회복될 때까지 조금 기다려 봐요.
examples.en: Let's wait a bit until the economy recovers.
The speed of recovery differs from person to person.

examples.ko: 잠을 잘 자야 피로가 회복되고 기분도 좋아져요.
examples.en: You need good sleep for fatigue to go away and your mood to improve.

explain: '낫다'는 병이나 상처에 주로 쓰고, '회복되다'는 체력·건강·경제·관계처럼 나빠졌던 것이 원래대로 돌아올 때 넓게 써요. '체력을 회복하다'는 내가 되찾는 느낌이고, '체력이 회복되다'는 저절로 좋아지는 느낌이에요. '감기가 회복되다'보다 '감기가 낫다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 낫다 is mainly for illness and wounds, while 회복되다 covers anything that got worse and returns to normal, such as stamina, health, the economy, or a relationship. 체력을 회복하다 feels like you win it back yourself, while 체력이 회복되다 feels like it happens on its own. For a cold, 감기가 낫다 sounds more natural than 감기가 회복되다.

examples.en: Right now safety comes before everything.

examples.ko: 시간이 없으면 중요한 일부터 우선해서 하세요.
examples.en: If you are short on time, do the important things first.
More people put health first these days.
I prioritized quality over price.
I will put family before work.

examples.ko: 응급 환자를 우선하고 다른 환자는 기다려요.
examples.en: Emergency patients come first and other patients wait.

explain: 대화에서는 '우선하다'보다 '먼저 하다', '먼저 챙기다'가 더 자주 나와요. '우선하다'는 뉴스, 안내문, 회의처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. '안전 우선', '고객 우선'처럼 명사 '우선'으로 줄여 쓰는 경우가 훨씬 많아요.
explain_en: In conversation people more often say 먼저 하다 or 먼저 챙기다. 우선하다 fits formal settings such as news, notices, and meetings. Even more common is the shortened noun form, as in 안전 우선 (safety first) and 고객 우선 (customer first).

examples.en: I bought a new phone case.
The color of this case is pretty.
Put your glasses in the case and keep them in the bag.

examples.ko: 케이스가 너무 커서 주머니에 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The case is too big to fit in my pocket.

examples.ko: 이 일은 특별한 케이스라서 먼저 물어봐야 해요.
examples.en: This is a special case, so I have to ask first.
Do I have to buy the charging case too?

explain: 휴대폰·안경·이어폰처럼 물건을 넣거나 씌우는 용품이 '케이스'예요. 휴대폰에 씌우는 건 '커버'라고도 불러요. '이런 경우'라는 뜻으로 '케이스'를 쓰기도 하지만 보통은 '경우'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: A 케이스 is an accessory you put things in or over, like phones, glasses, and earbuds. A phone case is sometimes called a 커버. People also use 케이스 for 'instance', but 경우 is usually more natural.

examples.en: The cake was divided into six pieces.
Our class splits into two teams.
If opinions split in two, we vote.
It is important that profits are shared fairly.
The room is divided by a curtain.

examples.ko: 열 개는 둘로 똑같이 나누어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Ten items can be split evenly into two.

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '나뉘다'라고 더 자주 해요. '나뉘어요', '나뉘었어요'처럼요. '나누다'는 내가 직접 가르는 행동이고, '나누어지다'는 저절로 또는 어떤 이유로 갈라진 상태예요.
explain_en: In speech it is often shortened to 나뉘다, as in 나뉘어요 and 나뉘었어요. 나누다 is something you do yourself, while 나누어지다 describes something that ends up split, on its own or for some reason.

examples.en: The picnic was cancelled because of rain.
What do I do if the flight gets cancelled?
The reservation was cancelled, so I changed it to another day.
It is a pity that so many shows are being cancelled.

examples.ko: 갑자기 취소된 약속 때문에 시간이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The plan that suddenly got cancelled gave me free time.
I got a text saying the class will be cancelled.

explain: 일정·예약·공연처럼 이미 정해진 일이 없던 일이 될 때 써요. 내가 직접 하면 '취소하다', 다른 이유로 그렇게 되면 '취소되다'예요. 약속이 갑자기 없어지는 일은 '펑크 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when something already planned, like a schedule, booking, or show, falls through. If you do it yourself it is 취소하다; if it happens for some other reason it is 취소되다. A plan that suddenly falls through is also called 펑크 나다 in casual speech.

examples.en: I stay away from sweet food for my health.
It is better to keep away from bad friends.
These days I am trying to stay away from my phone.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 사람들을 멀리하고 혼자 지내요.
examples.en: He keeps away from people and stays by himself.
I'm sorry that I kept my distance from my friend who had a cold.
Before an exam you have to stay away from games.

explain: '멀리하다'는 해롭거나 가까이하기 싫은 것을 일부러 피한다는 느낌이라서 사람·음식·습관에 써요. 반대말은 '가까이하다'예요. 단순히 거리가 먼 곳을 말할 때는 '멀다', '멀리 있다'를 써요.
explain_en: 멀리하다 carries the feeling of deliberately avoiding something harmful or unwanted, so it fits people, food, and habits. Its opposite is 가까이하다. For a place that is simply far away, use 멀다 or 멀리 있다.

examples.en: I separate the trash by type.
Separate paper and plastic before throwing them out.
Let's think about the two problems separately.
We separated the students by class.

examples.ko: 일과 생활을 분리하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to separate work from life.

examples.ko: 이 부분은 손으로 분리할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take this part off by hand.

explain: '분리수거', '분리배출'처럼 쓰레기를 버릴 때 가장 자주 들어요. '나누다'는 몫을 가르거나 이야기를 '나누다'처럼 폭이 넓고, '분리하다'는 붙어 있던 것을 떼어 놓는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '합치다', '결합하다'예요.
explain_en: You hear it most often with trash, as in 분리수거 and 분리배출. 나누다 is broad, covering splitting shares or 'sharing' a talk, while 분리하다 feels like pulling apart things that were attached. The opposites are 합치다 and 결합하다.

examples.en: My shoulders hurt, so I got a massage.
Sitting in a massage chair relieves my tiredness.
The massage felt so good that I got sleepy.
This hotel also has a massage service.
I showed my thanks to my grandmother with a massage.
Drink plenty of water after a massage.

explain: '안마 의자', '안마기'처럼 쓰는 말이고, 가게에서는 '마사지'라는 말도 같이 써요. 가족의 어깨를 풀어 드릴 때는 '주물러 드리다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It appears in words like 안마 의자 and 안마기, and shops also use the word 마사지. When you rub a family member's shoulders, you can also say 주물러 드리다.

examples.en: I often listen to pop music.
I heard a pop singer is coming to Korea.
This song mixes pop and K-pop.
Many of my friends study English through pop songs.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 팝을 들으면서 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I danced while listening to pop.
Do you like music other than pop too?

explain: '팝'은 혼자보다 '팝 음악', '팝 가수'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙을 때가 많아요. '팝송'은 보통 영어 노래를 가리키고, 한국 노래는 '가요'나 'K팝'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 팝 usually appears with another word, as in 팝 음악 and 팝 가수. 팝송 normally means English-language songs, while Korean songs are called 가요 or K팝.

examples.en: There is trust between us.

examples.ko: 신뢰를 얻으려면 약속을 잘 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: To earn trust you have to keep your promises.

examples.ko: 작은 거짓말 하나로 신뢰에 금이 갔어요.
examples.en: One small lie put a crack in the trust.

examples.ko: 한 번 깨진 신뢰는 다시 쌓기 어려워요.
examples.en: Trust that has been broken once is hard to rebuild.

examples.ko: 신뢰할 수 있는 사람과 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with someone I can trust.
Friendships are held together by trust.

explain: '믿음'과 뜻이 가깝지만, 신뢰는 회사·뉴스·정치처럼 조금 딱딱한 자리에서 더 잘 써요. 친구나 가족에게는 '믿음'이나 '믿다'를 더 자주 말해요. '신뢰를 얻다', '신뢰를 쌓다', '신뢰가 깨지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to 믿음, but 신뢰 suits slightly stiff settings such as business, news, and politics. With friends and family, people more often say 믿음 or 믿다. It pairs with fixed verbs: 신뢰를 얻다, 신뢰를 쌓다, 신뢰가 깨지다.

examples.en: I showed my friend around Seoul.
I want to take my child to see the zoo.

examples.ko: 외국 친구에게 부산을 구경시켜서 하루가 금방 갔어요.
examples.en: I showed my foreign friend around Busan, and the day flew by.
It is time to show the guests around the factory.
Next time, there are many places I can show you.
I showed my family around my office and they all liked it.

explain: '구경하다'는 내가 보는 것이고 '구경시키다'는 다른 사람이 볼 수 있게 해 주는 거예요. 보통 '구경시켜 주다', '구경시켜 드리다'로 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '보여 주다'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: 구경하다 is when you look around yourself, while 구경시키다 is letting someone else look around. It usually appears as 구경시켜 주다 or 구경시켜 드리다. 보여 주다 is also a common alternative.

examples.en: I go to a dance class every weekend.
That singer's dancing is really cool.

examples.ko: 댄스 연습 때문에 매일 늦게 집에 와요.
examples.en: Because of dance practice I come home late every day.
I am learning dance together with a friend.
This is a dance track, so it is fun.
Dance videos are very popular these days.

explain: '춤'이 원래 쓰던 우리말이고, '댄스'는 학원 이름이나 '댄스곡', '댄스 가수'처럼 합성어에서 자주 나와요. 동사는 '춤을 추다'라고 해야 하고 '댄스를 추다'는 어색해요. '방송 댄스', '재즈 댄스'처럼 종류 이름에도 댄스를 써요.
explain_en: 춤 is the native word, while 댄스 shows up in compounds like 댄스곡 and 댄스 가수, and in class names. For the verb you must say 춤을 추다; 댄스를 추다 sounds off. 댄스 is also used in genre names such as 재즈 댄스.

examples.en: I am the quiet type.
I like this type of clothes.

examples.ko: 이 휴대폰은 세 가지 타입으로 나와요.
examples.en: This phone comes in three types.
What type do you like?

examples.ko: 그 친구는 먼저 말을 거는 타입은 아니에요.
examples.en: My friend is not the type to talk first.

examples.ko: 이 두 사람은 타입이 완전히 달라요.
examples.en: These two people are completely different types.

explain: 사람의 성격이나 취향을 말할 때 '이런 타입', '내 타입'처럼 자주 써요. '내 타입이 아니에요'는 연애 상대로 취향이 아니라는 뜻으로 많이 들려요. 비슷한 '유형'은 글이나 발표에서 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: For personality or taste, people often say 이런 타입 or 내 타입. 내 타입이 아니에요 is commonly heard about someone who is not your romantic type. 유형, the similar word, is used more in writing and presentations.

examples.en: This city has very well-developed transportation.

examples.ko: 아이들은 어릴 때 뇌가 빨리 발달해요.
examples.en: Children's brains develop fast when they are young.
Technology advanced and life became easier.
For muscles to develop you need exercise and sleep.
The more developed a country is, the more hospitals it has.
The internet is developing at a really fast pace.

explain: '발전하다'는 앞으로 나아가 좋아지는 큰 흐름이고, '발달하다'는 몸·기술·제도가 단계를 거치며 자라는 느낌이에요. '교통이 발달하다', '기술이 발달하다'처럼 주어가 '교통·기술·산업·근육'일 때 특히 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 발전하다 is the big picture of moving forward and improving, while 발달하다 feels like a body, technology, or system growing step by step. It appears most often with subjects like 교통, 기술, 산업, and 근육.

examples.en: Our boss always comes to work early.
The boss suddenly called a meeting.
I beat the final boss in the game.
I told my boss about my vacation.
That person is the boss of this team.
He talks like a boss, so he is a bit scary.

explain: 회사에서 사장님이나 상사를 장난스럽게, 영어식으로 부르는 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '부장님', '팀장님'처럼 직함을 써요. 게임에서는 마지막에 싸우는 큰 적을 '보스'라고 불러요.
explain_en: In a company it is a playful, English-style way to refer to the CEO or a superior. When addressing someone directly, use a title like 부장님 or 팀장님. In games, 보스 is the big enemy you fight at the end.

examples.en: I go to a music festival in summer.

examples.ko: 이 페스티벌은 삼 일 동안 열려요.
examples.en: This festival runs for three days.
I bought film festival tickets in advance.
I am sad that the festival is over.
I went with friends to see the festival.
The roads are very jammed because of the festival.

explain: '축제'가 더 일상적인 우리말이고, 페스티벌은 음악·영화처럼 행사 이름에 붙을 때 많이 써요. '대학 축제', '지역 축제'는 축제를 써요. '록 페스티벌'처럼 이름이 정해진 행사는 페스티벌 그대로 불러요.
explain_en: 축제 is the more everyday native word, while 페스티벌 is common in event names for music and film. Say 대학 축제 and 지역 축제 with 축제. Events with fixed names, like a rock festival, keep 페스티벌.

examples.en: I put a pin in my hair.
The pin fell out and my hair came down.
I attached a name tag to my clothes with a pin.
Could you lend me just one pin?
Small pins are easy to lose.
I pricked my finger on a pin and it hurts.

explain: 머리에 꽂는 건 '머리핀', 옷에 다는 건 '옷핀'이라고 해요. 작고 뾰족한 물건을 널리 가리키지만 압정은 '압정'이라고 따로 불러요. 지도 앱에서 위치를 표시할 때 '핀 찍다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: A pin for your hair is a 머리핀 and one for clothes is an 옷핀. It covers small pointed things broadly, but a thumbtack has its own word, 압정. On map apps, people say 핀 찍다 for marking a location.

examples.en: The child is in a lot of pain after the shot.
He suffered for a long time after the breakup.
It looks like the puppy is hurting in its leg.

examples.ko: 친구가 너무 아파해서 병원에 같이 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend was in so much pain that I went to the hospital with them.

examples.ko: 너무 아파하지 마세요, 곧 괜찮아질 거예요.
examples.en: Try not to be so upset; you will be fine soon.

examples.ko: 아파할 때는 옆에서 말없이 있어 주세요.
examples.en: When someone is hurting, stay quietly by their side.

explain: '아프다'는 내 상태이고, '아파하다'는 다른 사람이 아픈 모습을 밖에서 보고 말할 때 써요. '나는 아파요'는 되지만 '나는 아파해요'는 어색해요. 몸뿐 아니라 마음이 아픈 사람에게도 써요.
explain_en: 아프다 describes your own condition, while 아파하다 is said about someone you observe being in pain. 나는 아파요 works, but 나는 아파해요 sounds odd. It is used for emotional pain as well as physical.

examples.en: The color of this outfit is really pretty.
What color do you like?
Please print it as a color photo.
Choose the color from black and white.
It is easy to find things if you sort by color.

examples.ko: 봄에는 밝은 컬러의 옷이 잘 팔려요.
examples.en: Bright-colored clothes sell well in spring.

explain: '색'이나 '색깔'이 일반적인 말이고, 컬러는 옷·인쇄·디자인처럼 상품 쪽에서 많이 써요. '컬러풀하다'는 알록달록하다는 느낌이에요. '색을 칠하다'는 되지만 '컬러를 칠하다'는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: 색 and 색깔 are the general words, while 컬러 is common in products, printing, and design. 컬러풀하다 gives a bright, many-colored feel. You can say 색을 칠하다 but almost never 컬러를 칠하다.

examples.en: I went to a gallery with a friend on the weekend.
This gallery has no admission fee.
The gallery is holding a new painting exhibition.
I need to clean up my phone's gallery.
We decided to meet in front of the gallery.
A small gallery opened in our neighborhood.

explain: 큰 전시 공간은 '미술관', 작고 그림을 파는 공간은 '갤러리'라고 불러요. 한국 휴대폰에서는 사진이 모인 앱도 '갤러리'예요. '사진첩'이라는 우리말도 있지만 요즘은 갤러리를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: A large exhibition space is a 미술관, while a smaller space that shows or sells art is a 갤러리. On Korean phones, the photo app is also called 갤러리. There is a native word 사진첩, but 갤러리 is more common now.

examples.en: The interviewer's question made me nervous.
That news puts everyone on edge.
Don't make me nervous, I'm starting to shake.
The teacher tried to keep the students on their toes on purpose.
Movies that keep you tense are fun.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 소리가 아이를 긴장시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: A sudden sound can make a child tense.

explain: '긴장하다'는 내가 떨리는 것이고 '긴장시키다'는 다른 사람이나 상황이 나를 떨리게 하는 거예요. 같은 뜻으로 '긴장하게 만들다'도 자주 말해요. 반대로 마음을 편하게 하는 건 '긴장을 풀다'예요.
explain_en: 긴장하다 is when you yourself get nervous, while 긴장시키다 is when another person or situation makes you nervous. 긴장하게 만들다 is a common alternative. The opposite is 긴장을 풀다, to relax.

examples.en: This insurance covers hospital bills.
I covered my gray hair with a hat.
I will cover that work for you.

examples.ko: 이 앱 하나로 모든 기능을 커버할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This one app can cover every function.
I tried to hide the blemish with makeup.
My friend covered for my mistake.

explain: '가리다'는 눈에 안 보이게 덮는 것이고, '커버하다'는 가리는 것 말고도 대신 메우거나 범위를 포함하는 뜻까지 넓게 써요. 회사에서 '제가 커버할게요'는 '제가 대신 맡을게요'라는 말로 자주 나와요. 다른 가수의 노래를 다시 부르는 것도 '커버하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 가리다 is to cover something so it can't be seen, while 커버하다 goes further to mean filling in for someone or including a range. At work, 제가 커버할게요 often means 'I'll take over for you'. Singing another artist's song is also called 커버하다.

examples.en: My parents enrolled me in a good school.
I am getting ready to enroll my child in elementary school.
I plan to enroll my daughter in kindergarten this year.
I felt relieved after getting my youngest enrolled.
I sent my child off to school, and the house got quiet.

examples.ko: 아들을 입학시키면 학부모 모임에 가야 해요.
examples.en: Once you enroll your son, you have to attend parents' meetings.

explain: '입학하다'는 학생이 학교에 들어가는 것이고 '입학시키다'는 부모나 보호자가 아이를 들어가게 하는 거예요. 그래서 주어가 부모예요. 학생이 주어일 때는 '입학했어요'라고 해요. 말할 때는 '학교에 보내다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: 입학하다 is when a student enters a school, while 입학시키다 is when a parent or guardian gets the child enrolled, so the subject is the parent. When the student is the subject, say 입학했어요. In speech, 학교에 보내다 is used more often.

examples.en: I listen to this artist's songs every day.
Who is your favorite artist?

examples.ko: 그 아티스트는 그림도 그리고 노래도 해요.
examples.en: That artist both paints and sings.
I met the artist in person and got an autograph.
It is a concert where artists gather in one place.

examples.ko: 젊은 아티스트와 함께 일해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with a young artist.

explain: 한국에서는 가수를 비롯해 음악이나 미술을 하는 사람을 폭넓게 '아티스트'라고 불러요. 팬들은 좋아하는 가수를 '아티스트'라고 부르기도 해요. 그림 그리는 사람은 '화가', 노래하는 사람은 '가수'처럼 구체적으로도 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea 아티스트 is used broadly for singers and anyone who does music or art. Fans often call their favorite singer an 아티스트. More specific words also exist: 화가 for a painter and 가수 for a singer.

examples.en: The title track on this album is really good.
The title match takes place tomorrow evening.
That athlete won the world title.

examples.ko: 게임을 켜면 타이틀 화면이 먼저 나와요.
examples.en: When you start the game, the title screen comes up first.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 올해 챔피언 타이틀에 도전해요.
examples.en: That team is going for the championship title this year.
The song picked as the title track is a different one.

explain: 책·영화·글의 이름은 '제목'이라고 하는 게 자연스러워요. '타이틀'은 앨범의 '타이틀곡', 스포츠의 챔피언 자리, 게임의 첫 화면처럼 정해진 곳에서 써요. 영화 이름을 물을 때는 '제목이 뭐예요?'라고 해요.
explain_en: For the name of a book, film, or text, 제목 is the natural word. 타이틀 is used in set contexts: an album's 타이틀곡, a championship in sports, and a game's first screen. To ask a film's name, say 제목이 뭐예요?

examples.en: My Korean level is still beginner.
We take a level test and decide the class.
I'm happy because my level went up in the game.
This book is divided by level.
To raise your level you have to practice every day.
Try choosing a class that fits your level.

explain: 한국어 학원에서는 '급'이나 '단계'라는 말도 같이 써요. 게임이나 반 나누기에서 '레벨'이 자주 나와요. 실력 차이를 말할 때 '레벨이 다르다'고 하면 차이가 크다는 느낌이에요. 일반적인 수준 이야기에서는 '수준'도 써요.
explain_en: Korean language schools also use 급 and 단계 alongside it. 레벨 comes up often in games and when sorting classes. Saying 레벨이 다르다 about skill implies a big gap. For general standards, 수준 is also used.

examples.en: The theme of this exhibition is autumn.

examples.ko: 테마 파티에 맞는 옷을 입고 갔어요.
examples.en: I went in clothes that fit the theme party.
This cafe has a unique theme.

examples.ko: 먼저 사진 테마를 정하고 나서 장소를 골랐어요.
examples.en: I first decided on the photo theme and then picked the location.
I made several works with the same theme.
I decorated the room to match the theme.

explain: 이야기나 발표의 중심 내용은 '주제'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 테마는 '테마파크', '테마 여행', '테마 카페'처럼 분위기나 콘셉트를 말하는 합성어에서 잘 나와요. 학교 발표나 토론에서는 '주제'를 써요.
explain_en: For the central idea of a story or presentation, 주제 is far more natural. 테마 appears in compounds about atmosphere or concept, like 테마파크, 테마 여행, and 테마 카페. In school presentations and debates, use 주제.

examples.en: This song is the biggest hit of the year.
That movie was a big hit.
To become a hit product, price matters too.
The singer has many hit songs, so I look forward to the concert.
This new product is sure to be a hit.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 히트 노래를 다 외웠어요.
examples.en: I memorized all of that singer's hit songs.

explain: '히트를 치다'처럼 '치다'와 함께 나오는 일이 많아서 '히트하다'보다 '히트를 치다'를 더 자주 들어요. '히트 상품', '히트곡', '히트작'처럼 앞뒤에 말을 붙여서도 많이 써요. '인기', '대박'과 비슷하지만 노래·영화·상품에 주로 써요.
explain_en: It often appears with 치다, so people hear 히트를 치다 more often than 히트하다. It also combines easily, as in 히트 상품, 히트곡, and 히트작. It is close to 인기 or 대박 but mainly applies to songs, films, and products.

examples.en: This drama became a hit overseas too.
I hope the new song becomes a hit.
Movies that become hits get sequels.
A small shop's idea became a hit and got famous.
It takes time for a song to become a hit.
I didn't know this book would be a hit.

explain: 노래·영화·상품이 크게 인기를 얻었을 때 써요. '히트(를) 치다'라고도 해요. 같은 뜻으로 '인기를 끌다'가 있고, '대박 나다'는 편한 사이에서 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a song, film, or product gets very popular. 히트(를) 치다 is another way to say it. 인기를 끌다 is an everyday alternative, and 대박 나다 is for casual conversation.

en: open and refreshing; bold and frank

examples.en: That actor has a bright, open smile.
She has an open, frank personality, so she has many friends.
Thank you for answering so frankly.
That singer's voice was clear and open.
Her wide, open eyes are impressive.

examples.ko: 시원스러울 만큼 큰 창문이 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the window that is so big it feels open and airy.

explain: '시원하다'는 온도·국물·기분에 널리 쓰지만, '시원스럽다'는 사람의 성격·표정·말투가 막힘없이 활짝 열린 느낌일 때 써요. 찬 음료나 바람에는 '시원스럽다'를 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 말로 '시원시원하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: 시원하다 is used widely for temperature, soup, and feelings, but 시원스럽다 describes a person's character, expression, or way of speaking that feels open and unblocked. It is not used for cold drinks or wind. A similar word is 시원시원하다.
